slides.title: Goal INTRODUCTION
slides.body:
GoalINTRODUCTION
During V&V activities on both vehicle and HIL, sometimes it is necessary to change signals
that ECUs send or receive on CAN bus. In some cases, the maneuvers to vary these
signals aren’t suitable to be replicated physically due to:
- Dangerous conditions for the driver
- Damages to vehicle components (sensors, actuators, wirings, ECUs)
- Difficult vehicular conditions
- Long-time or particular testing conditions
Others application cases could be:
- Loss of Communication (LoC) between real ECUs
- MC (Message Counter) and CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) errors (Implausibility Faults)
IG BLOCK and CAPL can be used for all those purposes

slides.title: Goal INTRODUCTION
slides.body:
GoalINTRODUCTION
On CAN Bus, different types of signals can be sent and received from ECUs:
- On Event (e.g. Diagnostic Frames)
- Cyclic On Event (e.g. Impact Frames)
- Cyclic
According to signals’ type, we can choose which type of gateway to be used
dt = frame’s cycle

slides.title: Goal IG BLOCK
slides.body:
GoalIG BLOCK
The Interactive Generator Block (IG) is used to create and send On Event messages ONLY.
WIRINGS’ SCHEME: T-CONNECTION
The IG node is in parallel with the CAN bus

slides.title: Goal IG BLOCK
slides.body:
GoalIG BLOCK
For this purpose, both a list of messages and trigger conditions are the input in a configuration
dialog. All the signals included in the selected messages are listed too and their values can be
freely changed, according to the associated CAN database (DBC of the architecture’s project
under testing). The main characteristic of the Interactive Generator Block is the possibility to
configure and interactively send messages during a running measurement (online).
Transmitted frame list
Signal list

slides.title: Goal IG BLOCK
slides.body:
GoalIG BLOCK
⮚ For each message, its parameters such as ID and DLC can be seen in the configuration window
⮚ The trigger conditions (Triggering) specify the instant of time the message will be sent
⮚ The content of the message (i.e. signals) can be changed in the Data Field (hex values) or in the
Signal list related to the frame (hex values or physical values)

slides.title: Goal COMMON USES OF CAPL
slides.body:
GoalCOMMON USES OF CAPL
⮚ To change the signal’s value of a specific cyclic and cyclic on event message
⮚ To set a Lost of Communication (LoC) between different ECUs
⮚ To set implausible data transmission/reception (MC, CRC, SNA or validity bit)
⮚ To change more signals of the same CAN bus at the same instant
⮚ To change signals belonging to different CAN buses (e.g. C1, ePT) → Double Gateway

slides.title: EXERCISES
slides.body:
⮚ Write a script in order to change a signal of a frame which contains CRC check
⮚ Write a script in order to change more signals of a frame which contains CRC check
⮚ Write a script in order to set implausible data through CRC corruption (i.e. sum number 10
to the CRC value calculated by the dedicated function)
⮚ Write a script in order to change two signals which belong to different messages
⮚ Write a script in order to change two signals which belong to different messages; the
second signal shall be changed after the first signal is modified (e.g. consider a time lap of
some seconds between the two modifications)
⮚ Try to send a diagnostic frame, monitor the request and the response in CANalyzer
